title: Buc-ee's first NC travel center is in the works. Here's what to expect - NewsBreak
text:
10 hours ago The Buc-ee's beaver mascot and local officials shovel dirt during a groundbreaking ceremony for a Buc-ee's travel center on Wednesday, June 10, 2026, off Exit 152 on Interstates 85 and 40 in Mebane. The Texas-based company plans to build a 74,000-square-foot store that could open by the end of 2027, featuring 120 fuel pumps, 650 parking spaces and 24 electric vehicle charging stations. Travis Long/tlong@newsobserver.com Buc-ee’s, the ultra-popular travel center chain, has kicked off construction on its first North Carolina location in Mebane. The 74,000-square-foot store is expected to open by the end of 2027.
FULL STORY: Buc-ee’s to break ground on its first NC travel center. Here’s when & where
Here are key takeaways:
A groundbreaking ceremony was held on Wednesday, June 10, at 1425 Trollingwood-Hawfields Road in Mebane. Mayor Ed Hooks, Mebane City Council members, Sen. Amy Galey and Reps. Dennis Riddell and Stephen Ross attended the event. The travel center will sit on 34 acres and include 650 parking spots, 120 gas pumps and 24 electric vehicle charging sites. Unlike many other Buc-ee’s locations, the Mebane store won’t have a car wash. Stan Beard, Buc-ee’s director of real estate and development, said in the release: “For our first North Carolina store, we’ve landed in the best location possible.” The store promises at least 200 full-time jobs with pay above minimum wage, 401k matching and paid vacation, according to a company news release. The opening date was pushed back from May 2027 to the end of 2027. Mebane City Council members approved site plans in 2024 amid criticism from the local community. The summary points above were compiled with the help of AI tools and edited by journalists. The full story in the link at top was reported, written and edited entirely by journalists.
